summary: The Improving Medicare Coverage Act amends the Social Security Act to lower the Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 50. It establishes a Medicare Cost Assistance Program to assist low-income individuals with Medicare premiums, coinsurance, and deductibles, shifting these functions from State Medicaid programs to Medicare. It also expands low-income subsidy access for Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage up to 200 percent of the federal poverty line and sunsets the entire law five years after it takes effect.

affected_groups.effect: Become eligible for Medicare coverage and enrollment periods.
Eligible for new Medicare cost assistance and expanded Part D prescription drug subsidies up to 200 percent of the poverty line.
Cease providing most Medicare cost-sharing benefits six months after enactment.

key_provisions: Amends the Social Security Act to lower the Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 50.
Creates the Medicare Cost Assistance Program to help eligible low-income individuals pay Medicare premiums, coinsurance, and deductibles.
Moves most Medicare cost-sharing benefits and administration away from State Medicaid programs into Medicare.
Expands Medicare Part D low-income prescription drug subsidies to individuals with incomes at or below 200 percent of the poverty line.
Authorizes $10 million in federal funding for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 for public awareness campaigns and grants to State health insurance assistance programs.
Sunsets and repeals the entire Act and its amendments five years after taking effect.
